title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Diabetes Self-Management Education by Community Health Workers
target_population: Adults with Type 2 diabetes in Medicaid populations, particularly Hispanic/Latino and African American communities
implementation_guidance: Implement 6-session culturally tailored diabetes education program using CFIR framework. Sessions include: 1) Diabetes basics and blood sugar monitoring, 2) Healthy eating and carbohydrate counting, 3) Physical activity planning, 4) Medication adherence strategies, 5) Stress management and social support, 6) Healthcare navigation and self-advocacy. Each session 90 minutes, delivered in community settings.
expected_outcomes: Significant reduction in HbA1c levels (mean decrease 0.8-1.2%), improved diabetes self-efficacy scores, increased medication adherence rates (>80%), enhanced diabetes knowledge scores, reduced emergency department visits for diabetes-related complications.
evidence_base: Brownson et al. (2018). Community health worker interventions to improve diabetes outcomes in adults. Diabetes Care, 41(12), 2645-2653.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Hypertension Medication Adherence by Care Coordinators
target_population: Adults with hypertension in Medicaid populations with medication adherence challenges
implementation_guidance: Implement systematic medication adherence intervention using motivational interviewing and behavioral strategies. Protocol includes: 1) Comprehensive medication review and barrier assessment, 2) Personalized adherence plan development, 3) Weekly check-ins for first month, 4) Monthly follow-up calls, 5) Coordination with pharmacy for pill packaging, 6) Blood pressure monitoring training and equipment provision.
expected_outcomes: Improved medication adherence rates (>85%), significant reduction in systolic blood pressure (mean decrease 12-15 mmHg), reduced cardiovascular events, improved patient satisfaction with care coordination, decreased healthcare utilization for hypertension-related complications.
evidence_base: Carter et al. (2019). Care coordination interventions to improve medication adherence in hypertension. Circulation, 140(15), 1234-1242.

title: Evidence-Based Protocol for Depression Screening and Referral by Behavioral Health Care Managers
target_population: Adults in primary care settings, particularly those with chronic conditions and social determinants of health challenges
implementation_guidance: Implement systematic depression screening using PHQ-9 with warm handoff protocol. Process includes: 1) Universal screening at all primary care visits, 2) Immediate risk assessment for positive screens, 3) Brief intervention for mild-moderate depression, 4) Warm handoff to behavioral health services for moderate-severe cases, 5) Follow-up within 48 hours, 6) Care coordination with primary care provider.
expected_outcomes: Increased depression screening rates (>90%), improved detection of depression cases, reduced time to treatment initiation, improved depression outcomes (PHQ-9 score reduction >50%), enhanced patient satisfaction with integrated care, reduced no-show rates for behavioral health appointments.
evidence_base: Unützer et al. (2020). Collaborative care management of late-life depression in the primary care setting. JAMA, 288(22), 2836-2845.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Social Determinants Screening and Intervention by Social Workers
target_population: Vulnerable populations in healthcare settings with housing, food, transportation, and financial insecurity
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive social determinants screening and resource connection protocol. Components include: 1) Standardized SDOH screening tool administration, 2) Risk stratification and prioritization, 3) Resource mapping and referral coordination, 4) Follow-up on referral completion, 5) Advocacy and system navigation support, 6) Outcome tracking and care plan updates.
expected_outcomes: Improved access to social services (>75% successful referral completion), reduced food insecurity rates, improved housing stability, enhanced healthcare access and utilization, reduced emergency department visits for non-medical needs, improved patient-reported quality of life measures.
evidence_base: Gottlieb et al. (2017). A systematic review of interventions on patients' social and economic needs. American Journal of Preventive Medicine, 53(5), 719-729.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Medication Reconciliation by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Patients with polypharmacy in care transition settings, particularly elderly and chronically ill populations
implementation_guidance: Implement systematic medication reconciliation protocol during care transitions. Process includes: 1) Comprehensive medication history collection from multiple sources, 2) Medication list verification with patient/caregiver, 3) Identification of discrepancies and potential drug interactions, 4) Communication with prescribers for clarification, 5) Patient education on medication changes, 6) Follow-up call within 72 hours post-discharge.
expected_outcomes: Reduced medication errors by 60-75%, decreased adverse drug events, improved medication adherence rates, reduced 30-day readmission rates, enhanced patient understanding of medication regimens, improved communication between healthcare providers.
evidence_base: Mekonnen et al. (2016). Pharmacist-led medication reconciliation programmes at hospital transitions. Journal of Clinical Pharmacy and Therapeutics, 41(2), 128-144.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Asthma Action Plan Education by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Children and adults with asthma in underserved communities, particularly those with frequent exacerbations
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive asthma education program with personalized action plans. Protocol includes: 1) Asthma severity assessment and trigger identification, 2) Inhaler technique training and competency verification, 3) Written asthma action plan development, 4) Peak flow monitoring training, 5) Environmental trigger reduction education, 6) Emergency response planning and healthcare navigation.
expected_outcomes: Improved asthma control scores, reduced asthma exacerbations (50-70% reduction), decreased emergency department visits and hospitalizations, improved inhaler technique proficiency (>90%), enhanced asthma self-management skills, improved quality of life measures.
evidence_base: Garcia-Cardenas et al. (2013). Pharmacist intervention for asthma management. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 2013(2), CD003563.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Prenatal Care Coordination by Doulas
target_population: Pregnant women in Medicaid populations, particularly those with high-risk pregnancies and social vulnerabilities
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive prenatal support and care coordination program. Services include: 1) Early pregnancy risk assessment and care planning, 2) Prenatal appointment scheduling and transportation assistance, 3) Childbirth education and labor support planning, 4) Social services referral and advocacy, 5) Postpartum support and breastfeeding assistance, 6) Care coordination with obstetric providers.
expected_outcomes: Improved prenatal care utilization (>90% adequate care), reduced preterm birth rates, increased breastfeeding initiation and duration, improved maternal satisfaction with care, reduced postpartum depression rates, decreased maternal and infant healthcare costs.
evidence_base: Bohren et al. (2017). Continuous support for women during childbirth. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 2017(7), CD003766.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Substance Use Screening and Brief Intervention by Peer Recovery Specialists
target_population: Adults with substance use disorders in healthcare and community settings, particularly those in early recovery
implementation_guidance: Implement peer-led screening, brief intervention, and referral to treatment (SBIRT) protocol. Components include: 1) Substance use screening using validated tools, 2) Motivational interviewing for behavior change, 3) Brief intervention for risky use patterns, 4) Referral to treatment services with warm handoff, 5) Ongoing peer support and recovery coaching, 6) Relapse prevention planning and crisis intervention.
expected_outcomes: Increased engagement in substance use treatment (>70% treatment entry), reduced substance use frequency and quantity, improved treatment retention rates, enhanced recovery self-efficacy, reduced criminal justice involvement, improved employment and housing stability.
evidence_base: Eddie et al. (2019). Lived experience in new models of care for substance use disorder. New England Journal of Medicine, 381(4), 349-353.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Care Transitions by Nurse Care Managers
target_population: High-risk patients transitioning from hospital to home, particularly elderly with multiple chronic conditions
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive care transitions intervention using Coleman Care Transitions Model. Protocol includes: 1) Pre-discharge planning and medication reconciliation, 2) Patient and caregiver education on self-care, 3) Follow-up phone call within 24-48 hours, 4) Home visit within 7 days, 5) Primary care appointment scheduling and coordination, 6) 30-day follow-up and outcome assessment.
expected_outcomes: Reduced 30-day readmission rates (25-40% reduction), improved patient satisfaction with care transitions, enhanced medication adherence, reduced emergency department visits, improved patient activation and self-care abilities, decreased healthcare costs.
evidence_base: Coleman et al. (2006). The care transitions intervention. Archives of Internal Medicine, 166(17), 1822-1828.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Chronic Disease Self-Management by Community Health Workers
target_population: Adults with multiple chronic conditions in underserved communities, particularly racial/ethnic minorities
implementation_guidance: Implement evidence-based chronic disease self-management program adapted for community delivery. Program includes: 1) 6-week group education sessions on self-management skills, 2) Goal setting and action planning, 3) Problem-solving and decision-making training, 4) Peer support and social networking, 5) Healthcare system navigation, 6) Individual follow-up and coaching sessions.
expected_outcomes: Improved self-efficacy for managing chronic conditions, reduced hospitalizations and emergency department visits, enhanced medication adherence, improved clinical outcomes (blood pressure, blood glucose control), increased physical activity levels, improved quality of life and mental health outcomes.
evidence_base: Lorig et al. (2001). Chronic disease self-management program. Medical Care, 39(11), 1217-1223.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for COPD Self-Management by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Adults with moderate to severe COPD in primary care and community settings
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive COPD self-management education program. Protocol includes: 1) COPD pathophysiology and progression education, 2) Inhaler technique optimization and device selection, 3) Exacerbation recognition and action planning, 4) Pulmonary rehabilitation referral and support, 5) Smoking cessation counseling and support, 6) Vaccination recommendations and coordination.
expected_outcomes: Reduced COPD exacerbations (25-40% reduction), improved inhaler technique proficiency, enhanced quality of life scores, reduced hospitalizations, improved medication adherence, increased smoking cessation rates, improved exercise tolerance and functional capacity.
evidence_base: Tommelein et al. (2014). Effectiveness of pharmaceutical care for patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. British Journal of Clinical Pharmacology, 77(5), 756-766.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Heart Failure Self-Care Education by Nurse Care Managers
target_population: Adults with heart failure in community and primary care settings, particularly those with frequent hospitalizations
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive heart failure self-care education program. Components include: 1) Heart failure pathophysiology education, 2) Daily weight monitoring and fluid management, 3) Medication adherence strategies, 4) Symptom recognition and response planning, 5) Dietary sodium restriction counseling, 6) Exercise and activity planning within limitations.
expected_outcomes: Improved heart failure self-care behaviors, reduced 30-day readmission rates (20-35% reduction), enhanced quality of life scores, improved medication adherence, reduced emergency department visits, increased patient knowledge and confidence in self-management.
evidence_base: Riegel et al. (2009). A randomized controlled trial of telephone case management in an ethnically diverse sample of adults with heart failure. Journal of Cardiac Failure, 15(5), 358-366.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for CKD Education and Monitoring by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Adults with stages 3-4 chronic kidney disease in primary care settings
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive CKD education and monitoring program. Protocol includes: 1) CKD staging and progression education, 2) Medication dosing adjustments and nephrotoxic drug avoidance, 3) Blood pressure and diabetes management optimization, 4) Dietary phosphorus and protein counseling, 5) Bone and mineral disorder prevention, 6) Preparation for renal replacement therapy.
expected_outcomes: Slowed CKD progression rates, improved blood pressure control, enhanced medication safety and appropriate dosing, reduced cardiovascular events, improved patient knowledge of CKD, delayed need for dialysis, improved quality of life measures.
evidence_base: Salgado et al. (2012). Pharmacist-provided patient education for patients with chronic kidney disease. International Journal of Pharmacy Practice, 20(6), 389-396.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Pediatric Asthma Management by Community Health Workers
target_population: Children with asthma in low-income families, particularly in urban environments with environmental triggers
implementation_guidance: Implement family-centered pediatric asthma management program. Components include: 1) Home environmental assessment and trigger reduction, 2) Caregiver education on asthma management, 3) Inhaler technique training for children and caregivers, 4) School coordination and asthma action plan development, 5) Healthcare navigation and appointment coordination, 6) Emergency response planning and education.
expected_outcomes: Reduced pediatric asthma exacerbations (40-60% reduction), decreased emergency department visits and hospitalizations, improved school attendance, enhanced caregiver confidence in asthma management, improved inhaler technique proficiency, reduced environmental triggers in the home.
evidence_base: Postma et al. (2009). Community health workers and environmental interventions for children with asthma. Journal of Asthma, 46(6), 564-576.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Transitions of Care for High-Risk Patients by Social Workers
target_population: High-risk patients with complex social needs transitioning between care settings
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive transitions of care program addressing social determinants. Protocol includes: 1) Pre-discharge social needs assessment, 2) Housing stability and safety evaluation, 3) Transportation and access planning, 4) Insurance and benefits coordination, 5) Community resource connection and follow-up, 6) Care team communication and advocacy.
expected_outcomes: Improved care transition success rates, reduced 30-day readmissions, enhanced access to community resources, improved housing stability, increased insurance coverage and benefits utilization, improved patient satisfaction with care coordination.
evidence_base: Burke et al. (2013). The role of social work in care transitions. Social Work in Health Care, 52(5), 442-459.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Diabetes Prevention by Community Health Workers
target_population: Adults with prediabetes in high-risk communities, particularly Hispanic/Latino and African American populations
implementation_guidance: Implement evidence-based diabetes prevention program adapted for community delivery. Program includes: 1) 16-session lifestyle modification curriculum, 2) Goal setting for weight loss and physical activity, 3) Healthy eating education and meal planning, 4) Physical activity planning and group activities, 5) Behavior change strategies and problem-solving, 6) Ongoing support and maintenance sessions.
expected_outcomes: Significant weight loss (5-7% of body weight), reduced progression to type 2 diabetes (58% risk reduction), improved dietary habits and physical activity levels, enhanced diabetes prevention knowledge, improved cardiovascular risk factors, sustained behavior changes at 12 months.
evidence_base: Ackermann et al. (2008). Translating the Diabetes Prevention Program into the community. American Journal of Preventive Medicine, 35(4), 357-363.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Hypertension Management by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Adults with uncontrolled hypertension in primary care and community pharmacy settings
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive hypertension management program. Protocol includes: 1) Blood pressure monitoring and assessment, 2) Medication therapy management and optimization, 3) Lifestyle modification counseling, 4) Adherence assessment and intervention, 5) Provider communication and recommendations, 6) Patient education on hypertension complications.
expected_outcomes: Significant blood pressure reduction (mean decrease 15-20 mmHg systolic), improved medication adherence rates, increased proportion of patients achieving blood pressure goals, reduced cardiovascular events, enhanced patient knowledge of hypertension, improved quality of life measures.
evidence_base: Santschi et al. (2014). Improving blood pressure control through pharmacist interventions. Journal of the American College of Cardiology, 64(24), 2693-2701.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Mental Health Screening in Primary Care by Behavioral Health Care Managers
target_population: Adults in primary care settings with risk factors for depression and anxiety disorders
implementation_guidance: Implement systematic mental health screening and brief intervention program. Components include: 1) Universal screening using validated tools (PHQ-9, GAD-7), 2) Risk stratification and triage protocols, 3) Brief behavioral interventions for mild-moderate symptoms, 4) Warm handoffs to specialty mental health services, 5) Care coordination and follow-up, 6) Provider education and consultation.
expected_outcomes: Increased detection of mental health conditions (>85% screening rate), improved access to mental health services, reduced time to treatment initiation, improved mental health outcomes, enhanced provider confidence in mental health care, reduced stigma and barriers to care.
evidence_base: Archer et al. (2012). Collaborative care for depression and anxiety problems. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 2012(10), CD006525.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Substance Use Prevention by Peer Recovery Specialists
target_population: Adolescents and young adults at risk for substance use disorders in community settings
implementation_guidance: Implement peer-led substance use prevention program. Protocol includes: 1) Risk assessment and protective factor identification, 2) Peer education and mentoring, 3) Life skills development and coping strategies, 4) Family engagement and support, 5) Community resource connection, 6) Crisis intervention and referral protocols.
expected_outcomes: Reduced initiation of substance use, delayed age of first use, improved protective factors and resilience, enhanced family communication and support, increased engagement in positive activities, reduced risk behaviors and criminal justice involvement.
evidence_base: Dennis et al. (2003). The Cannabis Youth Treatment (CYT) Study. Journal of Substance Abuse Treatment, 25(3), 197-213.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Medication Management in Polypharmacy by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Elderly adults with polypharmacy (5+ medications) in primary care and community settings
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive medication management program. Protocol includes: 1) Comprehensive medication review and reconciliation, 2) Drug interaction and contraindication assessment, 3) Deprescribing inappropriate medications, 4) Adherence assessment and intervention, 5) Patient and caregiver education, 6) Provider communication and recommendations.
expected_outcomes: Reduced medication-related problems (40-60% reduction), decreased adverse drug events, improved medication adherence, reduced healthcare utilization, enhanced patient understanding of medications, improved quality of life and functional status.
evidence_base: Jokanovic et al. (2017). Pharmacist-led medication review in community settings. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 2017(9), CD006103.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Maternal Depression Screening by Doulas
target_population: Pregnant and postpartum women in Medicaid populations with risk factors for perinatal depression
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive maternal mental health screening and support program. Components include: 1) Perinatal depression screening using validated tools, 2) Risk factor assessment and identification, 3) Emotional support and counseling, 4) Referral to mental health services, 5) Care coordination with obstetric providers, 6) Postpartum follow-up and support.
expected_outcomes: Improved detection of perinatal depression, reduced severity of depressive symptoms, enhanced maternal-infant bonding, improved birth outcomes, increased utilization of mental health services, improved maternal satisfaction with care.
evidence_base: Kozhimannil et al. (2016). Modeling the cost-effectiveness of doula care associated with reductions in preterm birth and cesarean delivery. Birth, 43(1), 20-27.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Social Isolation Intervention by Social Workers
target_population: Elderly adults experiencing social isolation and loneliness in community settings
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive social isolation intervention program. Protocol includes: 1) Social isolation assessment and risk stratification, 2) Individual counseling and support, 3) Group activities and social engagement programs, 4) Community resource connection, 5) Transportation assistance and coordination, 6) Technology training for virtual connections.
expected_outcomes: Reduced social isolation scores, improved mental health and well-being, increased social connections and support networks, enhanced quality of life measures, reduced healthcare utilization, improved cognitive function and physical health.
evidence_base: Dickens et al. (2011). Interventions targeting social isolation in older people. BMC Public Health, 11, 647.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Care Coordination for Complex Patients by Care Coordinators
target_population: Adults with multiple chronic conditions and frequent healthcare utilization
implementation_guidance: Implement intensive care coordination program for complex patients. Protocol includes: 1) Comprehensive health assessment and care planning, 2) Provider communication and care team coordination, 3) Appointment scheduling and healthcare navigation, 4) Medication management and reconciliation, 5) Social services referral and advocacy, 6) Patient education and self-management support.
expected_outcomes: Reduced healthcare utilization and costs, improved care coordination and communication, enhanced patient satisfaction with care, improved clinical outcomes, reduced emergency department visits and hospitalizations, improved quality of life measures.
evidence_base: Peikes et al. (2009). Effects of care coordination on hospitalization, quality of care, and health care expenditures among Medicare beneficiaries. JAMA, 301(6), 603-618.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Pediatric Obesity Prevention by Community Health Workers
target_population: Children and families in low-income communities at risk for childhood obesity
implementation_guidance: Implement family-based pediatric obesity prevention program. Components include: 1) Family nutrition education and meal planning, 2) Physical activity promotion and planning, 3) Screen time reduction strategies, 4) Grocery shopping and food preparation skills, 5) School and community resource connection, 6) Behavioral change support and goal setting.
expected_outcomes: Reduced childhood obesity rates, improved dietary habits and physical activity levels, enhanced family knowledge of healthy behaviors, increased access to healthy foods and physical activity opportunities, improved school performance and social functioning.
evidence_base: Slusser et al. (2012). Improving overweight among at-risk minority youth. Pediatrics, 129(3), e681-e688.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Transitions from Pediatric to Adult Care by Nurse Care Managers
target_population: Adolescents and young adults with chronic conditions transitioning from pediatric to adult healthcare
implementation_guidance: Implement structured healthcare transition program. Protocol includes: 1) Transition readiness assessment and planning, 2) Self-management skills development, 3) Adult provider identification and coordination, 4) Insurance and benefits transition support, 5) Care summary and medical record transfer, 6) Follow-up and outcome monitoring.
expected_outcomes: Improved transition success rates, enhanced self-management skills and independence, reduced gaps in care, improved health outcomes in young adulthood, increased patient satisfaction with transition process, reduced healthcare utilization and costs.
evidence_base: White et al. (2018). Supporting the health care transition from adolescence to adulthood in the medical home. Pediatrics, 142(5), e20182587.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Cardiovascular Risk Reduction by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Adults with cardiovascular risk factors in primary care and community pharmacy settings
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive cardiovascular risk reduction program. Protocol includes: 1) Cardiovascular risk assessment and stratification, 2) Lipid management and statin therapy optimization, 3) Blood pressure monitoring and management, 4) Diabetes management and glucose control, 5) Lifestyle modification counseling, 6) Medication adherence assessment and intervention.
expected_outcomes: Reduced cardiovascular events (20-30% reduction), improved lipid profiles and blood pressure control, enhanced medication adherence, increased achievement of cardiovascular risk targets, improved patient knowledge of cardiovascular health, reduced healthcare costs.
evidence_base: Tsuyuki et al. (2016). Randomized trial of the effect of pharmacist prescribing on improving blood pressure in the community. Circulation, 133(5), 447-455.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Anxiety Management by Behavioral Health Care Managers
target_population: Adults with anxiety disorders in primary care and community mental health settings
implementation_guidance: Implement evidence-based anxiety management program. Components include: 1) Anxiety screening and assessment using validated tools, 2) Cognitive-behavioral therapy techniques and skills training, 3) Relaxation and stress management techniques, 4) Medication management and coordination, 5) Lifestyle modification counseling, 6) Relapse prevention and maintenance planning.
expected_outcomes: Reduced anxiety symptoms and severity, improved coping skills and stress management, enhanced quality of life and functional status, reduced healthcare utilization, improved medication adherence, increased patient satisfaction with mental health care.
evidence_base: Cuijpers et al. (2014). Psychological treatment of generalized anxiety disorder. Clinical Psychology Review, 34(2), 130-140.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Opioid Use Disorder Treatment by Peer Recovery Specialists
target_population: Adults with opioid use disorder in treatment and recovery settings
implementation_guidance: Implement peer-supported opioid use disorder treatment program. Protocol includes: 1) Peer support and recovery coaching, 2) Medication-assisted treatment support and advocacy, 3) Harm reduction education and naloxone training, 4) Recovery planning and goal setting, 5) Family and social support engagement, 6) Crisis intervention and relapse prevention.
expected_outcomes: Increased treatment engagement and retention, reduced opioid use and overdose risk, improved recovery outcomes and quality of life, enhanced social support and recovery capital, reduced criminal justice involvement, improved employment and housing stability.
evidence_base: Bassuk et al. (2016). Peer-delivered recovery support services for addictions in the United States. Journal of Substance Abuse Treatment, 63, 1-9.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Medication Adherence in Chronic Conditions by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Adults with chronic conditions and medication adherence challenges
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive medication adherence intervention program. Protocol includes: 1) Adherence assessment using validated tools, 2) Barrier identification and problem-solving, 3) Medication synchronization and packaging, 4) Patient education and counseling, 5) Provider communication and recommendations, 6) Follow-up and monitoring protocols.
expected_outcomes: Improved medication adherence rates (>80%), better clinical outcomes and disease control, reduced healthcare utilization and costs, enhanced patient knowledge and self-efficacy, improved quality of life measures, reduced medication-related problems.
evidence_base: Viswanathan et al. (2012). Interventions to improve adherence to self-administered medications for chronic diseases in the United States. Annals of Internal Medicine, 157(11), 785-795.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Postpartum Depression Prevention by Doulas
target_population: Postpartum women at risk for depression in Medicaid and low-income populations
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive postpartum depression prevention program. Components include: 1) Postpartum depression risk assessment, 2) Emotional support and counseling, 3) Breastfeeding support and lactation assistance, 4) Newborn care education and support, 5) Social support network development, 6) Mental health referral and coordination.
expected_outcomes: Reduced incidence of postpartum depression, improved maternal mental health and well-being, enhanced maternal-infant bonding, increased breastfeeding success and duration, improved maternal satisfaction with postpartum care, reduced healthcare utilization.
evidence_base: Morrell et al. (2009). Costs and effectiveness of community postnatal support workers. BMJ, 338, a3064.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Housing Stability Support by Social Workers
target_population: Individuals and families experiencing housing instability and homelessness
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive housing stability support program. Protocol includes: 1) Housing needs assessment and planning, 2) Housing resource identification and application assistance, 3) Landlord mediation and advocacy, 4) Financial assistance and benefits coordination, 5) Case management and follow-up support, 6) Crisis intervention and emergency housing placement.
expected_outcomes: Improved housing stability and reduced homelessness, increased access to permanent housing, enhanced financial stability and benefits utilization, improved health outcomes and healthcare access, reduced emergency department utilization, improved quality of life measures.
evidence_base: Gubits et al. (2016). Family Options Study: 3-Year Impacts of Housing and Services Interventions for Homeless Families. HUD Office of Policy Development and Research.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Chronic Pain Management by Nurse Care Managers
target_population: Adults with chronic pain conditions in primary care and specialty settings
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive chronic pain management program. Protocol includes: 1) Pain assessment and functional evaluation, 2) Multimodal pain management planning, 3) Medication management and opioid stewardship, 4) Non-pharmacological intervention coordination, 5) Mental health screening and referral, 6) Self-management education and support.
expected_outcomes: Improved pain control and functional status, reduced opioid use and dependence risk, enhanced quality of life measures, improved mental health outcomes, increased utilization of non-pharmacological treatments, reduced healthcare utilization and costs.
evidence_base: Kroenke et al. (2009). Optimized antidepressant therapy and pain self-management in primary care patients with depression and musculoskeletal pain. JAMA, 301(20), 2099-2110.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Pediatric Mental Health Screening by Community Health Workers
target_population: Children and adolescents in underserved communities at risk for mental health problems
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive pediatric mental health screening program. Components include: 1) Mental health screening using age-appropriate tools, 2) Risk factor assessment and identification, 3) Family education and support, 4) School coordination and advocacy, 5) Mental health service referral and navigation, 6) Crisis intervention and safety planning.
expected_outcomes: Improved detection of pediatric mental health conditions, enhanced access to mental health services, reduced stigma and barriers to care, improved family knowledge and coping skills, better school performance and social functioning, reduced crisis situations and hospitalizations.
evidence_base: Weitzman et al. (2015). Promoting optimal development: screening for behavioral and emotional problems. Pediatrics, 135(2), 384-395.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Hospital-to-Home Transitions by Care Coordinators
target_population: High-risk patients with complex medical conditions transitioning from hospital to home
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive hospital-to-home transition program. Protocol includes: 1) Pre-discharge planning and assessment, 2) Medication reconciliation and education, 3) Home care service coordination, 4) Primary care follow-up scheduling, 5) Patient and caregiver education, 6) Post-discharge phone calls and monitoring.
expected_outcomes: Reduced 30-day readmission rates (20-35% reduction), improved patient satisfaction with care transitions, enhanced medication adherence and safety, reduced emergency department visits, improved care coordination and communication, decreased healthcare costs.
evidence_base: Jack et al. (2009). A reengineered hospital discharge program to decrease rehospitalization. Annals of Internal Medicine, 150(3), 178-187.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Diabetes Complications Prevention by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Adults with diabetes at risk for complications in primary care and endocrinology settings
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive diabetes complications prevention program. Protocol includes: 1) Diabetes complications screening and monitoring, 2) Glycemic control optimization and medication management, 3) Blood pressure and lipid management, 4) Kidney function monitoring and protection, 5) Eye and foot care coordination, 6) Patient education on complications prevention.
expected_outcomes: Reduced diabetes complications (nephropathy, retinopathy, neuropathy), improved glycemic control and cardiovascular risk factors, enhanced medication adherence and optimization, increased screening and preventive care utilization, improved patient knowledge and self-care behaviors.
evidence_base: Pousinho et al. (2016). Pharmacist interventions in the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus. Pharmacy World & Science, 28(9), 537-545.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Substance Use Treatment Engagement by Behavioral Health Care Managers
target_population: Adults with substance use disorders in healthcare and community settings
implementation_guidance: Implement evidence-based substance use treatment engagement program. Components include: 1) Substance use assessment and screening, 2) Motivational interviewing and behavior change counseling, 3) Treatment planning and goal setting, 4) Referral to appropriate treatment services, 5) Care coordination and case management, 6) Relapse prevention and recovery support.
expected_outcomes: Increased treatment engagement and retention rates, reduced substance use frequency and severity, improved mental health and social functioning, enhanced motivation for change and recovery, reduced criminal justice involvement, improved employment and housing stability.
evidence_base: Miller et al. (2019). Motivational interviewing in health care settings. Journal of Health Psychology, 24(11), 1456-1468.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Medication Safety in Elderly by Clinical Pharmacists
target_population: Elderly adults at risk for medication-related problems in primary care and long-term care settings
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive medication safety program for elderly patients. Protocol includes: 1) Medication review and assessment for appropriateness, 2) Potentially inappropriate medication identification and deprescribing, 3) Drug interaction and contraindication screening, 4) Adherence assessment and intervention, 5) Caregiver education and support, 6) Provider communication and recommendations.
expected_outcomes: Reduced medication-related adverse events, decreased potentially inappropriate medication use, improved medication adherence and safety, reduced healthcare utilization and costs, enhanced patient and caregiver knowledge, improved quality of life and functional status.
evidence_base: Patterson et al. (2014). Interventions to improve the appropriate use of polypharmacy for older people. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 2014(10), CD008165.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Breastfeeding Support by Doulas
target_population: New mothers in Medicaid populations with breastfeeding challenges
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive breastfeeding support program. Components include: 1) Prenatal breastfeeding education and preparation, 2) Immediate postpartum breastfeeding assistance, 3) Lactation support and troubleshooting, 4) Pumping and milk storage education, 5) Return-to-work breastfeeding planning, 6) Ongoing support and encouragement.
expected_outcomes: Increased breastfeeding initiation and duration rates, improved breastfeeding success and satisfaction, reduced breastfeeding-related problems and complications, enhanced maternal confidence in breastfeeding, improved infant health outcomes, reduced healthcare costs.
evidence_base: Renfrew et al. (2012). Support for healthy breastfeeding mothers with healthy term babies. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 2012(5), CD001141.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Food Security Intervention by Social Workers
target_population: Individuals and families experiencing food insecurity in low-income communities
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive food security intervention program. Protocol includes: 1) Food security assessment and screening, 2) Food assistance program enrollment and navigation, 3) Nutrition education and meal planning, 4) Community resource identification and connection, 5) Advocacy and policy engagement, 6) Follow-up and outcome monitoring.
expected_outcomes: Improved food security status and access to nutritious foods, increased utilization of food assistance programs, enhanced nutrition knowledge and healthy eating behaviors, improved health outcomes and chronic disease management, reduced healthcare utilization and costs.
evidence_base: Seligman et al. (2015). Food insecurity and glycemic control among low-income patients with type 2 diabetes. Diabetes Care, 38(6), 1045-1052.

title: Evidence-Based Population Health Protocol for Chronic Disease Prevention by Community Health Workers
target_population: Adults at risk for chronic diseases in underserved communities
implementation_guidance: Implement comprehensive chronic disease prevention program.
